newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bhuddist sect leader held in Belgian police raid.
newsitem.headline: Bhuddist sect leader held in Belgian police raid.

text.p: The Belgian leader of a Bhuddist-inspired sect was arrested on Saturday following raids on properties in the Belgian capital and in southern France, a Brussels court official said.
The 53-year-old man had been held since Friday after more than 200 Belgian police swooped on his Brussels villa.
Simultaneously, more than 100 French police with helicopter support raided a commune in Provence in southern France.
"Operation Sun", which covered raids on other Brussels properties, including two vegetarian restaurants, was the biggest joint Franco-Belgian police action, Belgian media said.

The raids, in which hundreds of documents were seized, were prompted by an official Belgian inquiry into alleged criminal activities of the Ogyen Kunzang Choeling (OKC) sect, which has an estimated 100 followers in Belgium and others in France, Portugal and Tahiti.
Charges against the leader were not disclosed, but he has been ordered to appear in court within five days.
Police said the sect was being probed in connection with a case of criminal association and the possible contravention of labour laws relating to the exploitation of illegal immigrants.
Another 60 sect members were earlier released in Brussels after questioning.
